summary_en: Voltage updated its capital efficiency targets to achieve ROIC and ROE of 5% and PBR above 1.0x, with an assumed cost of capital of 7–8%. Current metrics are negative due to operating losses; the company plans recovery through new business portfolio expansion and M&A including the acquisition of Opera House.
title_en: Response to Implement Management Conscious of Cost of Capital and Stock Price
translation_en_brief:
On October 29, 2026, Voltage announced updated targets for capital efficiency aligned with its assumed cost of capital of 7–8%. The company set near-term targets of ROIC and ROE at 5% and PBR above 1.0x, with longer-term aspirations for further improvement. Current performance is weak: as of June 2026, ROIC and ROE both turned negative due to operating and net losses, while PBR stood at 0.66x, down from 0.88x a year earlier.

The company attributes underperformance to ongoing transformation toward a three-pillar business model combining apps, digital comics, and consumer games. To recover, Voltage plans to accelerate growth in newer business segments, which reached 13.3% of revenue in the year ended June 2026 and are targeted to reach 20%. In July 2026, the company acquired Opera House via M&A to strengthen consumer game development, boost Asian sales, partner with external intellectual property, and expand publishing operations. Financial strategy includes maintaining appropriate equity while improving capital efficiency, reviewing low-margin businesses, and linking executive compensation to stock price performance and operating results to align management incentives with shareholder interests.
